result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-027.md for WF02-REQ-027 (event cancellation notifies every non-withdrawn registrant, once) at branch feature/WF02-REQ-027, commit 4a54482. Scope test: Step 2's artifacts_out (domain/registration.ts's selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent; handlers/event.ts's composeCancellationMessage, notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants, makeEventCancelHandler's new sender parameter and post-cancelEvent call site; index.ts's wiring; new i18n catalog keys) is real behavioral surface -- a real command handler sending real Telegram messages to a batch of real registrants. Full Steps 3b/4 apply.

Read core-directives.md, WF-02 Step 3, qa_testing_guide.md, docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-026.md as reference shape, docs/agents/design/REQ-027.md in full, and the real implementations directly: handlers/event.ts (composeCancellationMessage, notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants, makeEventCancelHandler), domain/registration.ts (selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent). Also read BACKEND-DEV's already-committed apps/bot/src/handlers/event.db.test.ts (5 tests, confirmed via git diff master...HEAD --stat and a direct full read) -- every one of those 5 calls notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants directly; none dispatches /event_cancel through a real bot.handleUpdate(). Confirmed via grep -rl "makeEventCancelHandler\|bot.command(\"event_cancel\"" apps/bot/src that no committed test anywhere in this repo dispatches this handler through grammY at all -- so every case in this spec drives the batch through a real bot.handleUpdate() dispatch of /event_cancel, per this run's task brief, making AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5's cases here independently valuable beyond re-running BACKEND-DEV's direct-call coverage: they additionally prove the full authorization -> cancelEvent -> notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants -> organizer-reply chain and its ordering, which no committed test currently exercises.

Per-AC design:
- AC1: own fixture, admission split 2 admitted/5 waitlisted/2 withdrawn (7 non-withdrawn), deliberately different from BACKEND-DEV's 3/2/1 and REVIEWER's independent 2/1/3 re-check. Real dispatch; asserts exactly 7 registrant sendMessage calls with zero to either withdrawn registrant, the organizer's own confirmation is the LAST captured call (ordering proof), exactly 7 ledger rows, and events.status = 'cancelled'.
- AC2 (judgment call, reasoning stated in the spec's own dedicated section): a same-process repeated-call test, NOT a genuine two-process kill-restart harness. Reasoning: (1) AC2's guarantee rests entirely on notification_ledger's existing unique index and sendLedgeredNotification's unchanged step-4 INSERT -- that exact primitive already has two independent genuine two-process proofs (REQ-025 AC1, REQ-026 AC3), and a third repetition against the same unchanged mechanism, only swapping the kind literal, would prove nothing new about REQ-027's own code. (2) REQ-027 has no scheduled/interval re-entry point like REQ-026's polled jobs -- notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants is invoked exactly once from a single command handler, so there is no restart-triggered auto-reinvocation scenario to prove immune to in-memory state the way REQ-026's AC3 needed to. (3) SECURITY-REVIEWER's structural finding (repeated trigger via the command surface is impossible -- events.status has no path back from 'cancelled', so a second /event_cancel is refused by the existing guard before reaching the batch) closes the 'double-cancel' half of AC2 entirely, leaving only 'the batch itself re-run by other means,' which a same-process repeat call models faithfully. This spec's AC2 case still adds real value over BACKEND-DEV's own (which calls the function directly twice): it dispatches the FIRST run through real bot.handleUpdate(), then repeats via a direct call, modeling the real chain once plus the residual scenario once.
- AC3: own fixture (2 registrants, one broadcast_opt_in=false), real dispatch, PLUS a structural grep -n "classification:" apps/bot/src/handlers/event.ts cross-check confirming the literal string (not a re-run of BACKEND-DEV's own assertion).
- AC4: own fixture including a pre-existing withdrawn row, real dispatch, full-row deep-equality before/after comparison (stronger than BACKEND-DEV's per-field admission-only spot checks), plus confirms events.status DID change to scope the comparison correctly.
- AC5: own fixture, own event title, lang='en' (BACKEND-DEV used the chapter-default 'ru') to independently prove the compose function reads the registrant's OWN resolved lang rather than a hardcoded/chapter-default one; exact-line-order assertion (stronger than toContain alone).
- New case, not present in BACKEND-DEV's file: non-organizer /event_cancel is refused. Judgment call (reasoning stated in the spec): added as new coverage, not a duplicate of REQ-016's own suite, because REQ-016's tests only cover checkOrganizerForChapter/requireOrganizerForChapter as pure domain functions (eventAuthorization.test.ts) and no committed test dispatches makeEventCancelHandler through a real bot at all, authorized or not -- this is the first such dispatch test for this handler, so closing the non-organizer gap here is the first opportunity to do so, not scope creep.

All cases in a single new committed file, apps/bot/src/handlers/event.dispatch.test.ts, own nextTgId=960_000_000+ range (confirmed distinct via grep -rn "nextTgId = " apps/bot/src against every existing file's range). Stated ISS-0014's --no-file-parallelism requirement for TEST-RUNNER.

Gap found while reading: no committed test anywhere dispatches makeEventCancelHandler through grammY, authorized or not -- this spec's new file closes that for both the happy path and the non-organizer path. No implementation defect found in handlers/event.ts or domain/registration.ts's REQ-027 additions while reading them directly -- nothing to file under ISSUE_QUEUE.md from this step.
